name: Dead Kennedys
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Jello Biafra ran for mayor of San Francisco, a Giger poster put him in a Los Angeles courtroom, and when the band split in 1986 the fights moved on to who owns the songs.

eras.title: From a classified ad to the ballot
eras.text: East Bay Ray ran a musician's ad in June 1978, and by July the band was opening at the Mabuhay Gardens. By November a Chronicle columnist was complaining about the name, and by the end of 1979 the singer was on the mayoral ballot.

years.h: [[East Bay Ray|d8559d8b-a8ee-4174-b5f1-226fe5e2891a]]'s ad in The Recycler finds its bassist
years.p: Ray, who'd played rockabilly in a band called Cruis'n, wanted bandmates. Bassist Klaus Flouride answered; singer [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]], drummer Ted and guitarist 6025 filled out the first line-up.

years.cap: Dead Kennedys at the Mabuhay Gardens, San Francisco, late 1970s
years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys
years.h: Dead Kennedys open for DV8 and Negative Trend at the Mabuhay
years.p: The Offs headlined on July 19, 1978. East Bay Ray says the band respects the Kennedy family and that the name stood for the death of the American Dream.
years.xp:
Early on, according to Wikipedia, the band also played as the DK's, the Sharks, the Creamsicles and the Pink Twinkies, because the name drew complaints. Ray's line on it: "the assassinations were in much more poor taste than our band." He counts John F. Kennedy, Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert F. Kennedy.

In November 1978 San Francisco Chronicle columnist Herb Caen wrote that "tastelessness has reached its nadir" with a band booked at the Mabuhay on November 22, the 15th anniversary of the JFK assassination. Per Wikipedia, the club's owner wouldn't cancel because of an existing contract.

years.src: Wikipedia: Carlo Cadona · Wikipedia: Live at the Deaf Club
years.h: Guitarist 6025 plays his last show at the Deaf Club
years.p: Carlo Cadona co-wrote songs like "Forward to Death" and "Ill in the Head" before leaving in March 1979. The tape of that night sat unreleased for 25 years.
years.xp:
Cadona joined a week before the first gig, according to Biafra, and Biafra later called him "the best all-around musician in the band." Biafra has said 6025's prog-rock leanings and unusual songwriting created friction with the rest of the band.

The March 3, 1979 set, with original drummer Ted on the kit, finally came out as Live at the Deaf Club on Manifesto Records on January 27, 2004, produced by Ray. Biafra criticized the release.

yt: Full set at the Mabuhay Gardens, October 10, 1979
years.h: A year of gig money pays for "California Über Alles"
years.p: Biafra and Ray start Alternative Tentacles to release it. The target is California governor Jerry Brown; the B-side is "The Man with the Dogs."

years.cap: Biafra and East Bay Ray at the Smilin' Buddha, Vancouver, June 14, 1979
years.src: SF Weekly · Wikipedia: Jello Biafra
years.h: Biafra takes fourth place in the San Francisco mayor's race
years.p: He collects 6,591 votes, 3.79 percent, in a ten-candidate field; Dianne Feinstein wins the runoff. His slogan, borrowed from a Jell-O ad, is "There's always room for Jello."
years.xp:
Biafra says Ted put the idea in his head, telling him he had such a big mouth he should run for mayor. Per SF Weekly, he wrote his platform on a napkin at a Pere Ubu show: businessmen in clown suits inside city limits, elected neighborhood police, Pier 39 demolished, a citywide car ban, and a statue of Dan White for pelting with eggs and produce.

When Feinstein staged a street-sweeping photo op in the Tenderloin, he answered by vacuuming leaves off her lawn.

eras.title: A drummer swap and a title the BBC can't say
eras.text: The debut album came out on Cherry Red in the UK, the drummer left for architecture school, and a single about a night out got banned from Radio 1 and still reached No. 36.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death
years.h: Biafra stops the band 15 seconds into a song at the Bammies
years.p: At the Bay Area Music Awards he tells the crowd, "We're not a punk rock band, we're a new wave band." Members pull black ties into dollar signs and play "Pull My Strings", a song mocking the music business.
years.xp:
The song Biafra cut off was "California Über Alles"; per Wikipedia his words were "Hold it! We've gotta prove that we're adults now."

The band played "Pull My Strings" only twice: once at the Bammies and once at the Mabuhay within a week, as Klaus Flouride recalled in 2017. The Bammies version was finally released on the 1987 compilation Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death.

years.src: Wikipedia: Holiday in Cambodia · Louder
yt: Holiday in Cambodia, official lyric video
years.h: A Thai massacre photo becomes the "Holiday in Cambodia" sleeve
years.p: The single, backed with "Police Truck", was written just after the Cambodian genocide and aimed at comfortable Western college kids. The sleeve photo is from the Thammasat University massacre in Thailand.
years.xp: Ray told Guitar World in 2025 that the song started as a jam in the rehearsal studio, part of his case that the band wrote together. Biafra's fight with his old bandmates over this same song, and whether it would sell jeans, comes 18 years later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fresh Fruit for Rotting Vegetables
years.h: Fresh Fruit for Rotting Vegetables comes out on Cherry Red
years.p: The cover shows burning police cars from the 1979 White Night riots. Trouser Press's Jon Young wrote that it "may be the only legitimate companion piece" to the Sex Pistols' debut.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Möbius Music in San Francisco in May and June 1980, and runs 33 minutes. It's the only Dead Kennedys studio album with Ted on drums.

It has gone gold in the US (500,000 units) and the UK (100,000), per Wikipedia. Not everyone agreed with Young: Robert Christgau gave it a C+ in the Village Voice. Biafra disliked the orange-tinted covers on early I.R.S. pressings.

years.cap: Dead Kennedys at the Commodore Ballroom, Vancouver, July 10, 1981
years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Fresh Fruit for Rotting Vegetables
yt: Holiday in Cambodia, live at Target Video (1981)
years.h: Ted leaves for architecture, and [[D.H. Peligro|af1735a0-8e58-41f7-a091-03d2578e9a51]] picks up the sticks
years.p: Ted, born Bruce Slesinger, plays his last show in February 1981. Peligro, who moved to San Francisco from St. Louis, sees the band, auditions and gets the job.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Ted announced in January 1981 that he wanted out to pursue architecture. Peligro went on to become the band's longest-serving drummer and stayed until he died in 2022.

years.src: Wikipedia: Too Drunk to Fuck · Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys
years.h: The charts print "Too Drunk To" and Radio 1 won't play it
years.p: "Too Drunk to Fuck" reaches No. 36 and tops the UK indie chart. Shops that won't stock it get stickers from the band.
years.xp:
The stickers told buyers they were "the victim of yet another stodgy retailer" afraid to reveal the title. Per Wikipedia it was the first UK Top 40 single with that word in its title. The B-side was "The Prey" and Geza X produced.

Wikipedia's accounts of what presenter Tony Blackburn said on air differ slightly between pages; one has him describing it as "a record by a group calling themselves The Dead Kennedys."

years.h: A free armband with a crossed-out swastika comes with "Nazi Punks Fuck Off"
years.p: Biafra wrote the song about violent punks at shows who he said were acting like Nazis. Anti-Racist Action later adopted the armband.

years.h: In God We Trust, Inc. has to be recorded twice
years.p: Eight songs cut on June 19 at Subterranean Studios were lost when the tape's oxide flaked off; the band redid them on August 22 at Möbius. The cover shows a gold Jesus on a cross of dollar bills.

eras.title: Fast, mean and running a label
eras.text: Plastic Surgery Disasters, Peligro's first full album, pushed the band toward hardcore. Then it mostly stopped recording so Biafra and Ray could run Alternative Tentacles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys
years.h: Plastic Surgery Disasters puts a World Press Photo winner on the cover
years.p: Thom Wilson produced the June 1982 sessions, Peligro's first full album with the band. Wikipedia says it's Biafra's favorite.
years.xp: The cover is Mike Wells's photograph of a withered Ugandan child's hand held in a white man's hand, taken in the Karamoja district. It won the World Press Photo award in 1980.

years.h: Alternative Tentacles finds a distributor in Mordam
years.p: The partnership began in 1983 and lasted until Mordam closed in 2009. Its owner, Ruth Schwartz, is later charged alongside Biafra in the Frankenchrist case.

years.cap: Biafra, East Bay Ray, Klaus Flouride and D.H. Peligro in a 1983 press photo
years.h: Two years of touring and no new album
years.p: Per Wikipedia, the band skipped recording in 1983 and 1984 to concentrate on Alternative Tentacles.

eras.title: The poster that outlasted the band
eras.text: Frankenchrist shipped with a Giger painting folded inside. A complaint, a police search and criminal charges followed, and the band split up in the middle of it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Frankenchrist
years.h: Frankenchrist comes with a cover the Shriners sued over
years.p: Biafra produced the third studio album at Hyde Street Studios in May and July 1985. Four Shriners pictured on the cover sued the band in 1986 over a photo Newsweek had published in the 1970s.
years.xp: The album mixes in trumpets and synthesizers, per Wikipedia. The Shriners' suit was only the first legal trouble the record brought.

years.src: Wikipedia: Frankenchrist
years.h: Biafra finds the Giger painting in a 1977 issue of Omni
years.p: H.R. Giger agrees to license "Landscape XX" for $600, half his usual fee. The band vetoes it for the cover, so it goes inside as a poster, with a warning sticker on the shrinkwrap.
years.xp: Biafra saw Giger's work in a 1977 Omni feature on a Paris art collection. He pitched it to his roommate and the band's artist, Jayed Scotti, and they went through Giger's New York agent, Les Barany, who negotiated a reproduction chrome. Scotti then made the production mechanicals by hand.

years.src: Diffuser · Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Jello Biafra
yt: Jello Biafra on the obscenity trial
years.h: Officers spend two and a half hours in Biafra's San Francisco home
years.p: Biafra says they took three copies of Frankenchrist, three spare posters and his private mail.
years.xp:
The case began in December 1985, when a teenage girl bought the album at a Wherehouse in Los Angeles County; Diffuser reports she was 14 and bought it for her 11-year-old brother. Her mother wrote to the California attorney general and Los Angeles prosecutors. Biafra says the complaint traced to the Parents Music Resource Center.

In June 1986 Biafra, Alternative Tentacles manager Michael Bonanno, Mordam's Ruth Schwartz, distributor Steve Boudreau and factory owner Salvatore Alberti were charged with distributing harmful matter to minors, which carried up to a year in county jail. Charges against Schwartz, Boudreau and Alberti were dismissed for lack of evidence. Sources give the raid as April 1986; one blog says April 15.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mutiny on the Bay · Wikipedia: Bedtime for Democracy
years.h: Biafra's last show with the band is at Freeborn Hall in Davis
years.p: A recording of the February 21, 1986 set later closes the live album Mutiny on the Bay. Wikipedia says the band had decided in January to split.
years.xp: The band also played The Stone in San Francisco on February 16 and 17, and those nights appear on the same 2001 live album. Sources differ on when the split became public: the Bedtime for Democracy Wikipedia page says the breakup was announced after that album's release.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Bedtime for Democracy
years.h: Bedtime for Democracy opens with "Take This Job and Shove It"
years.p: Recorded in April and July 1986 while the case hung over them. The title riffs on Ronald Reagan's film Bedtime for Bonzo.
years.xp: The cover art, per Wikipedia, shows a defaced Statue of Liberty overrun with Nazis, media, opportunists, Klansmen, corrupt officials and religious zombies.

eras.title: Seven to five, no verdict
eras.text: The band was over, but the case wasn't. A Los Angeles jury got it in August 1987, weeks after a compilation of unreleased tracks came out.

years.h: Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death sweeps up the leftovers
years.p: Unreleased tracks and alternate versions from 1979 to 1987, including the Bammies performance of "Pull My Strings". Wikipedia calls it the last Dead Kennedys album Biafra approved production of.
play: Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death

years.big: "Giger sees people the way Ramirez sees people."
q: Giger sees people the way Ramirez sees people.
years.src: Diffuser · Quartz · Wikipedia: Frankenchrist
yt: Jello Biafra interview at the trial, August 1987
years.h: A Los Angeles jury splits 7 to 5 for acquittal
years.p: Prosecutor Michael Guarino said it about painter H.R. Giger, comparing him to serial killer Richard Ramirez. After two days, jurors couldn't agree on Biafra and Michael Bonanno, and the judge wouldn't allow a retrial.
years.xp:
Guarino went on: "They are objects to hurt. They are not human." The defense argued that "Landscape XX," shown at museums in Vienna and the Bronx, was ugliness as social commentary, not obscenity. Judge Susan Isacoff ruled the poster had to be judged alongside the album's music and lyrics, and turned down a retrial: "I am not interested in developing a trial-and-error procedure for the prosecution."

Afterward, several younger jurors asked Biafra to sign their copies of the poster. Alternative Tentacles kept selling it by mail order with age verification, and the legal bills nearly bankrupted the label.

Diffuser says Guarino admitted in 1997 that he and his assistant were "a couple of young prima donna prosecutors" who realized midway through they were on the wrong side of history.

years.h: High Priest of Harmful Matter puts the trial on two discs
years.p: Biafra's 1989 spoken-word album has a censorship lecture on disc one and "Tales from the Trial" on disc two.

eras.title: Three bandmates sue the singer
eras.text: East Bay Ray, Klaus Flouride and D.H. Peligro outvoted Biafra on the catalog, then took him to court over unpaid royalties. Biafra says it was punishment for refusing a jeans ad; the band says it was about money. A jury and an appeals court sided with the band.

years.src: Justia · Snopes · The Moscow Times · Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles
years.h: The other three outvote Biafra on who runs the catalog
years.p: East Bay Ray, Klaus Flouride and D.H. Peligro vote Alternative Tentacles out as administrator. Decay Music, the four members' partnership since 1981, owns the songs; Biafra withheld royalties pending court approval, and the three sued in October 1998 for about $76,000.
years.xp:
Their claims, per Snopes and Wikipedia: Biafra conspired to pay lower royalty rates and hid what was owed, raised retail prices without raising the royalty calculation, and failed to promote the old catalog. In a 1999 ruling, a federal judge sent the case back to state court, finding the partnership claims weren't a copyright matter.

Biafra's side: Alternative Tentacles found an accounting error and corrected it before the suit. Ray's side: "He was picking money that was supposed to go to the Dead Kennedys and spending it on himself." Wikipedia also says Ray sold his stake in the label in the mid-1980s over "personal, financial and philosophical differences."

q: We tried our darndest to settle it.
years.src: NME · Deseret News · The Moscow Times · Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles
years.h: A San Francisco jury finds Biafra owes his old band about $220,000
years.p: The jury ruled against Biafra and Alternative Tentacles, and decided that Decay Music, not individual songwriters, owned the songs.
years.xp:
Biafra told the San Francisco Chronicle it was "the ugliest thing that's ever happened to me" and, per NME, that the band was punishing him for sticking to the band's principles. He said he'd consider an appeal.

The bandmates said they'd tried to settle. Wikipedia says the initial underpayment was an accounting error but the jury found he'd withheld information during negotiations. Reported totals vary between about $200,000 and $220,000; The Moscow Times says he'd also receive no royalties until paying the three another $140,000.

years.src: PopMatters · Snopes · Medium
years.h: Biafra says it's payback for refusing a Dockers ad
years.p: His account: the band wanted "Holiday in Cambodia" in a commercial and he said no. The band says no such request existed.
years.xp:
Biafra told PopMatters an ad agency proposed the song for a Dockers commercial, that he refused over Levi's layoffs and executive pay, and that the ad ran with a Pretenders song instead. He told another interviewer Ray asked, "Why don't you just go to the press and tell them we did it for charity?"

The band consistently denied it and called it a smokescreen; its lawyer, David Given, said the band "weren't down with it, and it never happened." Snopes rates the claim unproven, since neither jury nor judge ruled on what started the fight.

years.h: Mutiny on the Bay has Biafra's last show on it
years.p: Manifesto Records issues live sets from 1982 and 1986 eleven months after the verdict. Biafra criticized the release and later said he asked them to take his name off a live album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · PopMatters
years.h: Ray, Flouride and Peligro re-form with Brandon Cruz singing
years.p: Cruz, formerly of Dr. Know, sings from 2001 until May 2003. Biafra dismissed the new line-up as the world's greediest karaoke band.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia the band first played as "DK Kennedys" before going back to the full name. Flouride said in 2003 there hadn't been a show yet that people didn't really like. Biafra told PopMatters that Flouride was seen onstage in San Francisco saying they'd rehearsed only twice in thirteen years. In a 2012 Tampa Bay Times interview, Biafra said: "We haven't talked in a dozen years."

years.src: Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles · Wikipedia: Jello Biafra · PopMatters
years.h: Biafra loses his appeal, and most of the back catalog
years.p: He has to pay the outstanding royalties plus punitive damages and hand the majority of the catalog to Decay Music.
years.xp: Manifesto Records became the US licensee of the Dead Kennedys albums. Biafra described losing the catalog as "like getting some of your limbs blown off," per Wikipedia. His side: he said the ex-bandmates "never had to get jobs" while he kept the records in print for 22 years.

eras.title: Whose band is it now
eras.text: The reformed band has toured for two decades through three singers and licensed songs to films and games. Biafra objects to nearly all of it, and nobody has budged.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Too Drunk to Fuck
years.h: Songs go to a Hollywood remake and a skateboarding game
years.p: East Bay Ray, Klaus Flouride and D.H. Peligro license tracks to the 2004 film The Manchurian Candidate and to Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Ray says he received a fax from Alternative Tentacles indicating Biafra approved the game license. Biafra said of a later license, a Nouvelle Vague cover used in a 2007 scene of Robert Rodriguez's Planet Terror, that it went against everything the band stood for. The band told him to donate his share of the money to charity.

years.h: Ron "Skip" Greer takes over from Jeff Penalty
years.p: Penalty, who replaced Cruz in May 2003, left in March 2008 in what he called a "not amicable split." Greer, formerly of the Wynona Riders, has fronted the band since.

years.cap: East Bay Ray, Klaus Flouride, D.H. Peligro and Ron "Skip" Greer at Bottom Lounge, Chicago, June 27, 2014
years.src: Louder · Consequence · Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys
years.h: Riot Fest comes calling for a reunion, and Ray says Biafra declines
years.p: East Bay Ray said in 2017 that Riot Fest approached the band and that he and Klaus Flouride were interested.
years.xp: Ray repeated the claim in a May 2025 Guitar World interview: "It's Biafra that turns down any offers." He also said Biafra "got caught with his hands in the till and wants to blame us for getting caught." On songwriting he said the band wrote together and the chemistry made two plus two equal five. Biafra has said a reunion for nostalgia would go against what punk stands for.

years.src: NPR: D.H. Peligro · Consequence: Dead Kennedys Drummer
years.h: D.H. Peligro dies in Los Angeles at 63
years.p: An autopsy released May 2, 2023 found the combined effects of fentanyl and heroin, with non-small cell lung cancer present, not the head trauma first reported.
